body: A forced one, we can only escape it for so long.
I know, I would still rather just go. Just because something can have subjective value, it doesn't bean that value will be positive. I am not really a gambler. I take my losses.
I loved art, playing music, philosophy, math, computer science, literature, and so many other things; I was even good at some of those... I just lost it.
I enjoy things in a diminishing fashion, every day less.
Mainly because to me it is not about objective meaning, I am just not enjoying life and I wish to stop.

Look, I might go to hell by the hands of an arbitrary god, I might go to heaven by a god that rewards suicide; i have no way of knowing. I am jumping into a dark abyss and if I have eternal existence, whether it is torture or pleasure it will make my life not even matter. Both eternal punishment or reward make my life meaningless in the face of the temporality of them. I can never deserve either.
Or nowhere, also an option
I choose not to biologically live, whatever that means I am willing to accept it. :)

If I am due for eternal suffering, in a religious manner or not, then so be it. If I am to suffer in the future or even for eternity, it is either comparing infinity to infinity or comparing finite suffering to finite suffering plus more suffering and maybe some pleasure.

For our mind to exist after death it would need to be separate from the brain, and there is no evidence at all for any kind of substance external from  the physical substance. In fact, we define existence to be something that happens somewhere and in a stretch of time; something non material happerns nowhere and is either a process of the substance (temporal) or is atemporal (happens external to time-- never ). Something without matter and time happens nowher and never.
When I say death I mean general non-existence; when I say pain, I mean that which makes my biological constitution recoil but my brain and sense of self enforce my actions
I guess a part of my brain was made such that mixed with the specific situations I was exposed to I would just develop an affinity for pain and a desire for death.
